hook: A shovel of good farm soil holds more living things than there are people on Earth, and the dark top layer that feeds our crops took centuries to build. In the 1930s, after farmers plowed up the prairie grass of the southern Great Plains, a few dry, windy years carried that layer away in clouds of dust. Soil forms slowly and can disappear fast.

options: Moves water from leaves to the air
Builds new rock at the surface
prereq.why: Weathering breaks rock down by water, ice, temperature changes and living things, releasing minerals.

prereq.q: What do decomposers do in an ecosystem?
options: Break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil
prereq.why: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead organisms, releasing nutrients.

options: Water that flows over the land surface
Water that soaks into the ground
Water taken up by plant roots
prereq.why: Runoff is water moving over the surface toward streams; it carries soil with it.

figure.caption: A soil profile: the O horizon of organic matter, A (topsoil), B (subsoil), C (partly weathered parent material) and bedrock. Weathering works from below while organic matter is added from above.

chain.cause: Weathering breaks parent material (bedrock or deposited sediment) into small mineral particles
chain.effect: the mineral part of soil forms

chain.cause: Dead plants and animals are broken down by decomposers
chain.effect: humus forms and is mixed into the top of the soil

chain.cause: Water soaking down carries minerals and fine particles from the top layers
chain.effect: the soil sorts itself into horizons: O, A, B, C

chain.cause: Plants are removed and the soil is left bare
chain.effect: wind and water carry topsoil away, far faster than new soil forms

ideas: Soil forms from parent material (bedrock, or sediment carried by rivers, glaciers or wind) broken down by weathering, plus humus from decomposed organisms.
Climate, organisms, the shape of the land, the parent material and time control how fast soil forms. Warm, wet places weather rock and decompose matter fastest.
A soil profile has layers called horizons: O (organic matter), A (topsoil: humus and minerals), B (subsoil: minerals leached from above), C (partly weathered parent material), then bedrock.
Erosion is the removal and transport of soil by wind and water. Plant roots hold soil and plant cover shields it, so bare soil erodes fastest.
Eroded soil fills streams with sediment, carries nutrients and pesticides with it, and leaves farms with poorer subsoil.

misconception.wrong: Soil keeps forming, so losing some to erosion is quickly made up.
misconception.right: New soil does form, but only over centuries: a few centimeters can take hundreds of years to form, but a bare field can lose that much in a few years.

summary: Soil forms slowly from weathered parent material and humus from decomposed organisms, and it sorts into horizons: O, A (topsoil), B (subsoil), C and bedrock. Warm, wet climates form soil fastest. Wind and water erode soil, fastest where plants are removed and the ground is bare, and eroded soil harms both the land it leaves and the streams it reaches.
